name: Computing, Ph.D.
department: College of Computing, Engineering and Construction — School of Computing

deadline.value: June 1 is the recommended international Fall application deadline in the UNF Graduate Catalog (August 1 general Fall deadline on the Graduate School deadlines page, which defers to international deadlines). Important: the Computing Ph.D. webpage currently notes admission of international students on F-1 visas (or seeking F-1 status) is closed pending SEVP approval.
deadline.quote: The recommended deadline for international students for most programs are: | Fall - June 1 | Spring - October 1 | For programs with fall deadlines earlier than June 1 and spring deadlines earlier than October 1, the international deadlines are the same as the program deadlines.

also.quote: Computing (PhD) | Deadlines | Fall | August 1 | Spring | December 1 | Summer | April 15 | *International Applicants: Please see the program webpage for international application deadlines.
Admission of international students on F-1 visa (or seeking such status) is currently closed pending SEVP approval.

gre_general.value: GRE Verbal (>= 150) and GRE Quantitative (>= 155) scores are required for admission to the Computing Ph.D.
gre_general.quote: Application Requirements | In addition to the general Graduate School application requirements, the application materials for the Computing PhD program must include the following: | GRE verbal and quantitative scores | A minimum score of 150 in the GRE verbal section | A minimum score of 155 in the GRE quantitative section

gre_subject.value: No ETS GRE Subject Test exists for this field (ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics, and Psychology).
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Pre-application supervisor commitment is not required; students identify a dissertation supervisor and form a 4-member dissertation committee by completion of 30 post-bachelor credits.
supervisor.quote: The student must form a dissertation committee and identify a dissertation supervisor, who is a Graduate Faculty member and will chair this committee, by the completion of 30 credits in the program (post Bachelor).

funding.value: Competitive departmental graduate assistantships ($2,500/semester for 10 hrs/wk or $5,000/semester for 20 hrs/wk, plus prorated tuition waiver and out-of-state fee waiver for >=10 hr/wk appointments; renewal not guaranteed; international students eligible) and university fellowships (Key Bradbury STEM Fellowship $10,000/yr up to 2 years; Milligan Presidential Fellowship $5,000/yr).
funding.quote: Graduate assistants receive a stipend based on their appointment: | $2,500 per semester (fall and spring) for 10 hours per week (minimum) | $5,000 per semester (fall and spring) for 20 hours per week (minimum) | Tuition waivers are prorated based on your appointment hours. | Availability depends on departmental needs and funding, so it’s important to connect with your program directly to learn about current opportunities. | Some assistantships may be renewed, but renewal is not guaranteed.

also.quote: The Key Bradbury STEM Fellowship is awarded to outstanding University of North Florida graduate students. This fellowship provides one student in a field related to science, technology, engineering or math (STEM) $10,000 per academic year ($5,000 per semester; fall/spring) for up to two years as long as the student remains eligible.

entry_route.value: 72-credit post-baccalaureate Ph.D. admitting applicants with a four-year bachelor's degree (GPA >= 3.0 in last 60 credits) and allowing up to 30 relevant graduate transfer credits or graduate GPA consideration for prior graduate degree holders.
entry_route.quote: A four-year baccalaureate degree from a regionally accredited U.S. institution, or its equivalent from a foreign institution, with a GPA of 3.0 or higher in all work attempted in the last 60 credit hours of undergraduate study. | If the applicant has a graduate degree in a Computing field, graduate courses may be considered if the undergraduate GPA is less than 3.0 | A minimum of 72 credits beyond the baccalaureate degree | Student may transfer a maximum of 30 relevant graduate credits toward the coursework requirement.

notes: Offers two concentrations: Cybersecurity and Intelligent Systems (AI, Machine Learning, Data Analytics, Data Mining, Text Mining; cross-listed under datasci). F-1 VISA RESTRICTION: Program page states 'Admission of international students on F-1 visa (or seeking such status) is currently closed pending SEVP approval.' Applicants without a prior Computing degree must complete undergraduate prerequisite coursework (Programming, Data Structures, Applied Discrete Math, Databases, Computer Networks). Requires 3 letters of recommendation, resume, and <=500-word statement of purpose.
